In 1945, a chicken in Colorado lived for eighteen months without its head.
A farmer named Lloyd Olsen was getting chicken ready for dinner, and swung the axe.
But Mike didn't die. He got up, and kept walking around like nothing had happened.
He even tried to peck for food, and preen his feathers.
The next morning, he was still alive. So Olsen decided to keep him.
He fed Mike with an eyedropper, dropping milk, water and grain straight down his throat.
The axe had missed the main vein in his neck, and a blood clot stopped him from bleeding out.
Most of his brain stem was left behind, and in a chicken, that part runs the heartbeat, breathing, and walking.
Mike became a star. He toured the country, appeared in Life magazine, and earned up to four thousand five hundred dollars a month.
Scientists at the University of Utah examined him, to make sure it wasn't a hoax.
Then, in 1947, he choked in a motel room. The syringe used to clear his throat had been left behind at the last show.
Today, his hometown of Fruita throws a festival for him every year.
It's called the Mike the Headless Chicken Festival.
